title: Select [Aliases (AS)]
description:
## Aliases
Aliases let you rename columns and tables in your query. They don't change the actual data - just how it appears in results.

### Column aliases:
```sql
SELECT name AS employee_name, salary AS pay
FROM staff;
```

### Table aliases (useful for JOINs):
```sql
SELECT e.name, d.name
FROM employees AS e
INNER JOIN departments AS d
    ON e.dept_id = d.id;
```
Way shorter than writing `employees.name` and `departments.name` every time.

---
## Assignment:
BWS has a new `invoices` table. Select the customer_name as `customer`, amount as `total`, and status as `payment_status`.
setupCode: CREATE TABLE invoices (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_name TEXT, amount REAL, status TEXT); INSERT INTO invoices VALUES (1, 'Steve', 3.47, 'unpaid'), (2, 'Bob', 1500.00, 'paid'), (3, 'Alice', 750.50, 'pending'), (4, 'Steve', 0.99, 'unpaid');
expectedOutput:
customer | total | payment_status
Steve | 3.47 | unpaid
Bob | 1500 | paid
Alice | 750.5 | pending
Steve | 0.99 | unpaid
